problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize F(w)=n⁻¹∑ᵢ log Eξ∼lawᵢ[exp(scoreᵢ(w,ξ))] over a nonempty closed convex domain. Each sampled score satisfies a supporting-subgradient inequality, implying convexity of the scores and F. Differentiability and smoothness are not required.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositionalEntropicRisk.lean: objective; spec.admissible, domain conditions and score supporting inequality.

problem_class.label: composite
problem_class.details: Nested nonlinear composition log E exp(score), rather than an additive smooth-plus-proximable decomposition.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: The objective averages n≥1 entropic-risk terms, each containing an expectation under its own hidden probability law.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositionalEntropicRisk.lean: Params.n and nonzero; Instance.law; normalizer; objective.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A sample query at w returns a uniform random index i and two conditionally independent sampled score/subgradient pairs for that same i. These are subgradients of sampled scores, not an unbiased gradient oracle for F. The caller cannot select i or reuse the hidden sample at another point.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositionalEntropicRisk.lean: Query.sample; Reply.sample; Seed; sampleLaw; sampleOracle; spec.admissible supporting inequality.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: Each sampling reply includes two sampled score values; neither the normalizer nor the objective value is returned.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Exact metric projection onto the hidden domain is available as a separate query. Sampling and projection queries consume the same oracle budget; one sampling query returns both pairs.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositionalEntropicRisk.lean: Query.projection; sampleOracle; spec.admissible projection inequalities. LongTails/Template.lean: Algorithm.query; executeWithTrace; _run.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniformly over i and feasible w, writing Zᵢ(w)=E exp(scoreᵢ(w,ξ)), the assumptions are E‖gradᵢ(w,ξ)‖²≤G², E exp(2 scoreᵢ(w,ξ))≤κ Zᵢ(w)², and E[exp(2 scoreᵢ(w,ξ))‖gradᵢ(w,ξ)‖²]≤σ² Zᵢ(w)². These are second-moment bounds, not a centered variance bound for an unbiased objective-gradient oracle; σ=0 is permitted.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositionalEntropicRisk.lean: normalizer; spec.valid; spec.admissible, three moment inequalities.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is a second-countable real Hilbert space with its Borel measurable structure, without a finite-dimensional restriction. Scores lie pointwise in [c0,c1]. Oracle seeds are IID across calls, and the two samples are independent conditional on their shared index. A minimizer exists within distance R of feasible w0; no domain-diameter bound is assumed. All Params are public, including n, B≥1, c0≤c1, G>0, κ≥1, σ≥0, R≥0 and ε>0; scores, subgradients, laws and domain are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/CompositionalEntropicRisk.lean: Params; Instance; sampleLaw; spec.publicInput, valid and admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID.measurable, independent and marginal.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The measurable output ŵ must have an integrable objective gap satisfying E[F(ŵ)−F(w*)]≤ε for a domain minimizer w*.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The output belongs to the domain for every outcome, not merely almost surely.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Accuracy is in expectation over the joint algorithm and oracle randomness under a fixed oracle-call budget; no high-probability objective-gap guarantee is required.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: An established entropic-risk formulation with a specialized paired-sampling oracle, normalized exponential moment bounds, general Hilbert-space geometry, and a shared sampling/projection budget. This classification does not assert novelty. Repository proofs and implementations were not inspected; no qualifying reference verified here is not evidence that none exists.

descriptionHtml:
Compositional Entropic Risk Minimization

We minimize F(x)=n−1∑i=1nlog⁡Eξ∼νi[esi(x,ξ)] over a nonempty closed convex set C in a separable real Hilbert space E, where n≥1, νi are probability laws, and si are bounded convex sample scores. Measurable score subgradients satisfy second-moment and exponentially weighted moment bounds, and a given starting point lies near a minimizer x⋆∈C. The oracle returns two independent score–subgradient pairs for one uniformly sampled component, or an exact projection onto C. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable, everywhere feasible output x¯ with integrable gap and E[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε, averaging over independent algorithm and oracle randomness.

Let Ξ be a measurable sample space, and write si:E×Ξ→R,gi:E×Ξ→E,Zi(x)=Eξ∼νi[esi(x,ξ)],F(x)=1n∑i=1nlog⁡Zi(x). The optimization problem is minx∈CF(x). The norm is induced by the inner product on E. The parameters satisfy n,B∈N,n≥1,B≥1,c0,c1∈R,c0≤c1,G>0,κ≥1,σ≥0,R≥0,ε>0. The algorithm receives E, Ξ, n, B, c0, c1, G, κ, σ, R, ε, and the starting point x0; the scores, subgradients, laws, and feasible set are accessed through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Feasible set and initial distance). The set C⊆E is closed and convex, and x0∈C. There exists x⋆∈C such that F(x⋆)≤F(x)for every x∈C,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Assumption 2 (Bounded scores and subgradients). For each i∈{1,…,n}, the maps si and gi are jointly measurable. For every ξ∈Ξ and x,y∈C, si(x,ξ)+⟨gi(x,ξ),y−x⟩≤si(y,ξ),c0≤si(x,ξ)≤c1. Thus gi(x,ξ) is a subgradient of the sample score on C.

Assumption 3 (Moment bounds). For each i∈{1,…,n} and x∈C, the function ξ↦∥gi(x,ξ)∥2 is integrable under νi, and Eξ∼νi[∥gi(x,ξ)∥2]≤G2,Eξ∼νi[e2si(x,ξ)]≤κZi(x)2,Eξ∼νi[e2si(x,ξ)∥gi(x,ξ)∥2]≤σ2Zi(x)2.

Queries may be made at any point of E. At a sampling query x, a component I is drawn uniformly from {1,…,n}. Conditional on I=i, two samples ξ and ξ′ are drawn independently from νi. The reply is (I, (sI(x,ξ),gI(x,ξ)), (sI(x,ξ′),gI(x,ξ′))). Each score and its subgradient use the same sample, and the two pairs share the component index. The draws used at successive calls are independent and identically distributed, and independent of the algorithm’s randomness.

At a projection query x, the oracle returns ΠC(x). The map ΠC:E→E is measurable and satisfies ΠC(x)∈Cfor every x∈E,⟨x−ΠC(x),u−ΠC(x)⟩≤0for every x∈E, u∈C. Sampling and projection queries share one total call budget; a sampling call returns both pairs above.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and belong to C for every realization. Its objective gap must be integrable and satisfy EP[F(x¯)−F(x⋆)]≤ε, where P is the joint law of the independent algorithm and oracle randomness, and x⋆ is a fixed minimizer on C.

Minimize F(w)=n−1∑i=1nlog⁡mi(w) over a nonempty closed convex set W in a separable real Hilbert space, where mi(w)=∫esi(w;ξ)dpi(ξ). Jointly measurable scores and subgradients satisfy si(w;ξ)∈[c0,c1], si(y;ξ)≥si(w;ξ)+⟨gi(w;ξ),y−w⟩, and, uniformly on W, ∫∥gi∥2dpi≤G2, ∫e2sidpi≤κmi2, ∫e2si∥gi∥2dpi≤σ2mi2. Here n,B≥1, G>0, κ≥1, σ,R≥0, ε>0, and w0,w⋆∈W, with w⋆ minimizing F and ∥w0−w⋆∥≤R. The oracle provides exact projection and IID uniform-anchor draws, each with two conditionally independent score–subgradient samples from pi. Target: ∫[F(w¯(ω))−F(w⋆)]dP(ω)≤ε under the IID execution law P; (1) constructs the SCENT average.

import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Uniform
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.Pi
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Basic

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace BigOperators

namespace LongTails.Setups.CompositionalEntropicRisk

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [linearE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [completeE : CompleteSpace E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  [countableE : SecondCountableTopology E]
  Ξ : Type
  [measurableΞ : MeasurableSpace Ξ]
  n : ℕ
  [nonzero : NeZero n]
  B : ℕ
  c0 : ℝ
  c1 : ℝ
  G : ℝ
  κ : ℝ
  σ : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  w0 : E

attribute [instance] Params.normedE Params.linearE Params.completeE Params.measurableE
  Params.borelE Params.countableE Params.measurableΞ Params.nonzero

structure Instance (q : Params) where
  score : Fin q.n → q.E → q.Ξ → ℝ
  grad : Fin q.n → q.E → q.Ξ → q.E
  law : Fin q.n → ProbabilityMeasure q.Ξ
  domain : Set q.E

noncomputable def normalizer {q : Params} (I : Instance q) (i : Fin q.n) (w : q.E) : ℝ :=
  ∫ ξ, Real.exp (I.score i w ξ) ∂(I.law i : Measure q.Ξ)

noncomputable def objective {q : Params} (I : Instance q) (w : q.E) : ℝ :=
  (q.n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, Real.log (normalizer I i w)

inductive Query (q : Params) where
  | sample : q.E → Query q
  | projection : q.E → Query q

inductive Reply (q : Params) where
  | sample : Fin q.n → ℝ × q.E → ℝ × q.E → Reply q
  | projection : q.E → Reply q

abbrev Seed (q : Params) := Fin q.n × (Fin q.n → q.Ξ) × (Fin q.n → q.Ξ)

noncomputable def sampleLaw {q : Params} (I : Instance q) : Measure (Seed q) :=
  (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin q.n)).toMeasure.prod
    ((Measure.pi fun i => (I.law i : Measure q.Ξ)).prod (Measure.pi fun i => (I.law i : Measure q.Ξ)))

noncomputable def sampleOracle {q : Params} (I : Instance q) (projection : q.E → q.E)
    (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → Seed q)) : Oracle (Query q) (Reply q) where
  Seed := fun _ => Seed q
  law := P
  answer := fun _ (_, query) seed => match query with
    | .sample w => .sample seed.1
        (I.score seed.1 w (seed.2.1 seed.1), I.grad seed.1 w (seed.2.1 seed.1))
        (I.score seed.1 w (seed.2.2 seed.1), I.grad seed.1 w (seed.2.2 seed.1))
    | .projection x => .projection (projection x)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance := Instance
  Query := Query
  Reply := Reply
  Output q := q.E
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.B ∧ q.c0 ≤ q.c1 ∧ 0 < q.G ∧ 1 ≤ q.κ ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q I O :=
    ∃ (projection : q.E → q.E) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → Seed q)),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (ξ : ℕ → Seed q) => ξ k)
      (sampleLaw I) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = sampleOracle I projection P ∧
    Convex ℝ I.domain ∧ IsClosed I.domain ∧ q.w0 ∈ I.domain ∧
    Measurable projection ∧
    (∀ x, projection x ∈ I.domain) ∧
    (∀ x, ∀ u ∈ I.domain, ⟪x - projection x, u - projection x⟫ ≤ 0) ∧
    (∀ i, Measurable (Function.uncurry (I.score i))) ∧
    (∀ i, Measurable (Function.uncurry (I.grad i))) ∧
    (∀ i ξ, ∀ x ∈ I.domain, ∀ y ∈ I.domain,
      I.score i x ξ + ⟪I.grad i x ξ, y - x⟫ ≤ I.score i y ξ) ∧
    (∀ i ξ, ∀ x ∈ I.domain, q.c0 ≤ I.score i x ξ ∧ I.score i x ξ ≤ q.c1) ∧
    (∀ i, ∀ x ∈ I.domain, Integrable (fun ξ => ‖I.grad i x ξ‖ ^ 2) (I.law i : Measure q.Ξ)) ∧
    (∀ i, ∀ x ∈ I.domain, (∫ ξ, ‖I.grad i x ξ‖ ^ 2 ∂(I.law i : Measure q.Ξ)) ≤ q.G ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ i, ∀ x ∈ I.domain, (∫ ξ, Real.exp (2 * I.score i x ξ) ∂(I.law i : Measure q.Ξ)) ≤
      q.κ * (normalizer I i x) ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ i, ∀ x ∈ I.domain, (∫ ξ, Real.exp (2 * I.score i x ξ) * ‖I.grad i x ξ‖ ^ 2
      ∂(I.law i : Measure q.Ξ)) ≤ q.σ ^ 2 * (normalizer I i x) ^ 2) ∧
    (∃ wstar ∈ I.domain, IsMinOn (objective I) I.domain wstar ∧ ‖q.w0 - wstar‖ ≤ q.R)
  successful q I output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ (∀ ω, output ω ∈ I.domain) ∧
    ∃ wstar ∈ I.domain, IsMinOn (objective I) I.domain wstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => objective I (output ω) - objective I wstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, objective I (output ω) - objective I wstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.CompositionalEntropicRisk
